title: Analyst, Evergreen Portfolio Management - Private Debt
role_summary_en: Analyst in StepStone Group's Private Debt Portfolio & Risk Management team in Zurich, supporting evergreen funds through corporate-lending/private-debt data processing, market research, portfolio and performance analysis, and day-to-day fund-management support.
company_profile: StepStone Group is a global private-markets investment firm (Nasdaq: STEP). As of 30 Jun 2026 it reported about USD 913bn of total capital responsibility and USD 245bn AUM across 31 offices. Its Private Debt platform has about USD 73bn of capital responsibility and 75+ investment professionals, covering corporate, real-estate, infrastructure and specialty credit.
role_profile: Private Debt Portfolio & Risk Management analyst focused on evergreen funds. Core work is portfolio/performance analysis, market research, transaction-data processing and support to senior investment professionals rather than pure deal origination. Prior private-markets/private-debt experience is preferred, not mandatory. English fluency is required and other languages are only a plus, so there is no German-language blocker. FIT: strong investment/private-markets adjacency; main trade-off is portfolio/risk/analytics versus direct underwriting/origination.
salary_research: Research 23 Aug 2026: recent StepStone Group Analyst submissions in Zurich on Glassdoor show total pay around CHF 92-108k and CHF 97-113k; broader Zurich StepStone data show Analyst roughly CHF 75-105k and Senior Analyst roughly CHF 105-115k. For this private-debt Analyst role, a reasonable expectation is about CHF 95-110k total cash, with base likely around CHF 85-100k plus bonus. I would target CHF 100k base / CHF 110k+ total and ask how bonus and pension are structured. This is company-specific Zurich evidence, not a generic Swiss benchmark.
